argentina||Social security: Employer contributions run about 26.4% of payroll across pensions, family allowances, the national employment fund and health insurance (obra social), on top of the separate 6% healthcare contribution.
australia||Social security: There is no general social security payroll tax. The employer obligation is the superannuation guarantee — 12% of ordinary time earnings paid into the employee's fund — plus state payroll tax above each state's threshold and workers' compensation premiums by industry.
barbados||Overtime: Overtime is paid at one and a half times the normal rate beyond the standard 40-hour week, and at double time on a public holiday or a rest day.
Barbados Employment Rights Act; Shops Act
barbados||Probation: There is no statutory probation period. Probation is set in the contract, commonly three months, and the Employment Rights Act's unfair-dismissal protection starts after one year of continuous service.
belgium||Maternity leave: 15 weeks — up to 6 before the birth and at least 9 after — or 17 weeks for multiples. The employer pays the first week at full salary; the mutual insurance fund pays 82% for the next weeks and 75% after that, on a capped daily wage.
belgium||Sick leave: The employer pays guaranteed salary for the first month of illness for white-collar employees; after that the health insurance fund (mutuelle) pays. Blue-collar rules differ in the first weeks.
belgium||Notice period: Notice runs on seniority alone since the 2014 Unified Status Act — not age, salary or job grade — and is counted in weeks starting the Monday after notice is given. It scales from one week under three months of service upward, and a May 2026 act caps employer notice at 52 weeks for contracts starting on or after 1 July 2026. From 1 August 2026 a one-week notice applies both ways during the first six months. Resignation notice is capped at 13 weeks.
Unified Status Act; Belgian act of May 2026; Liedekerke
belgium||Severance: An employer can end the contract with notice or pay an indemnity in lieu covering the same period, calculated on the employee's annual pay including benefits. With the 2026 cap, that indemnity tops out at the equivalent of 52 weeks for contracts starting on or after 1 July 2026.
Belgian Employment Contracts Act; CMS dismissal guide, 2026
bolivia||Social security: Employer contributions total about 17.2% of payroll: roughly 10% to the health fund (Caja de Salud), 1.71% for professional risk and provident housing, plus a 3% employer solidarity contribution to the pension system. The employee separately pays about 12.7% into their AFP account.
Bolivian social security schedules; Trading Economics employer contribution table, 2026
brazil||Minimum wage: R$1,621 per month as of 1 January 2026, up from R$1,518 — about R$54.04 a day or R$7.37 an hour.
brazil||Social security: INSS employer contribution is 20% of payroll, plus RAT work-accident insurance of 1% to 3% by risk class and about 5.8% of third-party levies (Sistema S). FGTS adds 8% deposited monthly into the employee's fund. Total mandatory employer cost lands around 28% to 36% of gross before the 13th salary and the vacation third.
INSS/FGTS schedules; teamed. Brazil cost breakdown, 2026
brazil||Healthcare: There is no employer health-insurance mandate — public care runs through SUS, funded by general taxation. Private medical cover (plano de saúde) is nonetheless close to universal in formal employment and is expected in any competitive offer; where a collective agreement covers the role, it can be compulsory.
Brazilian Constitution art. 196; collective agreement practice
brazil||Retirement: The state pension (RGPS) is funded by the INSS contributions above and paid by the government. Private supplementary pensions (previdência privada) are voluntary and employer-sponsored plans are common at larger employers.
british-virgin-islands||Social security: Social security is split evenly, about 4.5% each from employer and employee on insurable earnings, and the National Health Insurance levy is likewise split, at about 3.75% each.
BVI Social Security Board; NHI Ordinance
canada||VAT: 5% federal GST, rising to 13% or 15% HST in the provinces that harmonised, with Quebec adding QST separately.
canada||Social security: CPP and Employment Insurance, both employer-matched. For 2026 the employer pays 5.95% of pensionable earnings between $3,500 and $74,600, plus 4% CPP2 on earnings up to $85,000, and EI at 1.4 times the employee premium — roughly $4,650 per employee at the ceiling before salary.
chile||Minimum wage: CLP 553,553 per month for workers aged 18 to 65, retroactive to 1 May 2026, up from CLP 539,000 in January.
chile||Social security: Withheld from pay: about 10% to the employee's AFP pension account plus the AFP commission, 7% for health through FONASA or an ISAPRE, and 0.6% unemployment insurance on indefinite contracts. The employer pays 2.4% unemployment insurance on indefinite contracts, 3% on fixed-term ones, and from August 2026 a further 3.5% pension contribution under the reform.
colombia||Social security: Employer contributions total about 20.5% of salary: 12% to pension, 8.5% to health, plus parafiscal levies to SENA, ICBF and the family compensation fund.
czech-republic||Social security: The employer pays 24.8% social security — 21.5% pensions, 2.1% sickness, 1.2% unemployment — plus 9% health insurance, so 33.8% in total. The employee pays 7.1% plus 4.5% health. Social security stops at a 2026 ceiling of CZK 2,350,416; health insurance has no cap.
dominican-republic||Social security: Employer contributions are about 7.1% to the pension system (SCI), 7.09% to family health insurance (SFS) and a labour-risk premium of about 1.2%.
dominican-republic||Sick leave: Sick pay runs through the family health insurance branch of social security (SFS) after a waiting period, with the employer covering the first days.
el-salvador||Social security: Employer contributions are about 7.5% to ISSS for health, on top of the 8.75% AFP pension contribution paid separately by the employer.
finland||Minimum wage: No statutory minimum wage. Pay floors come from the collective agreement covering the sector, and those are generally binding across it.
finland||Social security: Employer contributions total about 20.8% of payroll, dominated by the TyEL earnings-related pension, with health insurance, unemployment insurance and accident cover on top.
finland||Maternity leave: Pregnancy leave is 40 working days, usually starting 30 weekdays before the due date. Parental leave then gives each parent 160 working days, up to 63 of which can be transferred. Kela pays the allowance.
Finnish family leave reform, in force since 2022; Kela, 2026
france||Minimum wage: SMIC is €1,867.02 gross per month since 1 June 2026, after €1,823.03 from January — €12.02 gross an hour at 35 hours a week.
france||Social security: Employer contributions are among the heaviest in Europe at roughly 45% of gross pay, covering health, pension, family allowances, unemployment and the mandatory mutuelle.
germany||Minimum wage: €13.90 gross per hour since 1 January 2026, up from €12.82 — roughly €2,409 a month at a 40-hour week. It rises to €14.60 in January 2027.
germany||Social security: Employer contributions are about 19.4% of gross, split roughly evenly with the employee across statutory health, pension, long-term care and unemployment insurance, each capped at its own ceiling.
greece||Minimum wage: €920 gross per month from 1 April 2026, up from €880 — €41.09 a day for general workers.
guatemala||Social security: The employer pays about 12.67% of wages to IGSS for illness, maternity, accidents and the pension programme, and the employee pays 4.83%. Employers also pay roughly 1% each to IRTRA for recreation and INTECAP for training.
honduras||Minimum wage: Set by sector and employer size rather than as a single national figure, and renegotiated periodically between government, employers and unions.
honduras||Social security: Employer contributions run about 12% to 13% of pay: roughly 7% to IHSS for health, maternity, disability and pension, 1% to 1.5% to the RAP private pension scheme, and 1% to INFOP for vocational training. IHSS and RAP are capped at monthly salary ceilings; INFOP is not.
hungary||Social security: The employer pays the 13% social contribution tax on gross wages; the employee carries 18.5% across pension and health.
india||Minimum wage: Set by each state and by skill category rather than nationally, so the floor differs by state, industry and whether the work is classed as unskilled, semi-skilled or skilled.
india||Social security: The employer's main contribution is 12% of wages to the Employees' Provident Fund, matched by the employee, with ESI health cover on top for lower-paid workers and gratuity accruing separately.
indonesia||VAT: 12% headline, but 11% in effect for ordinary goods and services — the 12% rate applies to a reduced base of 11/12 of the price. The full 12% applies to luxury goods.
PP No. 1 Tahun 2025; Cabinet Secretariat of Indonesia
ireland||Minimum wage: €14.15 per hour for workers aged 20 and over from 1 January 2026. Lower rates apply by age: €12.74 at 19, €11.32 at 18.
ireland||Social security: Employer PRSI is about 11.25% of pay above the lower threshold, with a reduced rate on low earnings.
israel||Social security: Employer national insurance is about 7.6%, and on top of it the employer must fund the mandatory pension and severance components — roughly 6.5% pension and 8.33% severance — so the true load is materially higher than the national insurance rate alone.
Trading Economics employer contribution table, 2026; Israeli pension order
italy||Minimum wage: No statutory minimum wage. The applicable national collective agreement (CCNL) sets minimum pay by sector and job grade.
italy||Social security: Employer contributions are about 30% of gross to INPS across pension, unemployment, sickness and family allowances, with TFR accruing separately at about 8.33% a year.
italy||Notice period: Set by the sector's national collective agreement (CCNL), not by a single statutory table: it runs on job classification (operai, impiegati, dirigenti) and seniority, typically from about 15 days up to several months. Law 604/1966 sets the floor; the CCNL is the operative rule.
italy||Severance: TFR is deferred pay, not a dismissal payment: about 8.33% of annual gross accrues each year and is paid to every departing employee whatever the reason, resignation included, usually with the final payslip within 30 to 45 days.
Italian Civil Code art. 2120; TFR practice, 2026
jamaica||Social security: Employer contributions are about 12.5% of pay across NIS, the education tax, HEART training levy and NHT housing.
jamaica||Probation: No statutory probation period. Probation is set in the contract, commonly three months, and unfair-dismissal protection under the Employment (Termination and Redundancy Payments) Act attaches with continuous service.
Jamaican Employment (Termination and Redundancy Payments) Act
japan||Social security: Employer social insurance is about 16.4% of remuneration across health, nursing care, employees' pension, employment insurance and workers' accident compensation.
japan||Retirement: Employees' Pension Insurance (kosei nenkin) is mandatory and employer-matched: 9.15% each side, 18.3% combined, on standard monthly remuneration capped at JPY 650,000 and on bonuses capped at JPY 1,500,000 per payment. Company retirement allowances are common on top, but those are voluntary.
malaysia||Minimum wage: RM1,700 per month, in force since February 2025 and applying in all states including Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan — about RM8.18 an hour.
malaysia||Social security: Employer contributions are about 13% of wages to EPF for most earners, plus SOCSO and the employment insurance system.
mexico||Social security: Employer contributions run roughly 30% to 40% on top of base pay, calculated on the integrated wage (SBC) rather than base salary: IMSS across sickness, risk, disability and childcare, INFONAVIT housing at 5%, the SAR retirement contribution rising to about 3.15% in 2026 under the pension reform, plus a state payroll tax of about 2% to 4.25% depending on the state.
netherlands||Minimum wage: €14.99 gross per hour for workers 21 and over since 1 July 2026, after €14.71 in January. Since 2024 the Netherlands sets a single hourly minimum with no statutory monthly figure.
netherlands||Social security: Employer contributions are roughly 20% of pay across unemployment, disability and the health insurance levy, with sector pension contributions on top where a mandatory fund applies.
new-zealand||VAT: 15% GST, unchanged since 2010. Long-term accommodation is taxed at a reduced 9%; exports are zero-rated.
new-zealand||Minimum wage: NZD 23.95 an hour from 1 April 2026, up from NZD 23.50. Training and starting-out rates are NZD 19.16.
new-zealand||Social security: There is no broad social security payroll tax. The employer pays the KiwiSaver contribution of at least 3% for enrolled employees and the ACC work levy set by industry risk.
new-zealand||Maternity leave: Up to 26 weeks of government-funded paid parental leave for the primary carer, paid by Inland Revenue, capped at NZD 811.05 a week from 1 July 2026. Employees with 12 months' service can take up to 52 weeks of leave in total, unpaid beyond the 26.
Parental Leave and Employment Protection Act; Inland Revenue, 2026
nicaragua||Social security: INSS carries the load on the employer: about 21.5% to 22.5% of payroll depending on headcount, covering health, disability, old age and workplace risk, against roughly 7% from the employee. Employers also pay a 2% INATEC training levy.
panama||VAT: ITBMS at 7%, with higher rates on alcohol, tobacco and hotel services.
panama||Social security: The employer pays about 12.25% to the Caja de Seguro Social plus 1.5% Seguro Educativo, so roughly 13.75% before professional-risk insurance, which runs between about 1% and 5.7% depending on the industry. The CSS rate rises to 14.25% in March 2027 under Law 462.
panama||Probation: The first three months are treated as the trial period, during which either side can end the contract without the notice and indemnity that apply afterwards.
paraguay||Social security: Employer contributions are about 16.5% of pay to IPS, covering health, maternity, pensions and workplace risk.
peru||Social security: The employer pays about 9% of pay to EsSalud for health cover; the pension contribution of about 13% is withheld from the employee and goes to a private AFP or the state ONP.
philippines||Notice period: Thirty days' written notice for an authorised-cause dismissal — redundancy, retrenchment, closure, labour-saving devices or disease — with a copy filed at the DOLE regional office. A just-cause dismissal instead follows the two-notice rule: a notice to explain, a hearing, then a notice of decision.
Labor Code of the Philippines; DOLE
philippines||Severance: Separation pay is owed on authorised-cause dismissals only, whatever the length of service: one month's pay per year of service for redundancy or labour-saving devices, half a month per year for retrenchment or closure. Dismissal for just cause carries none.
poland||Social security: Employer contributions are about 20.5% of gross across pension, disability, accident and the labour fund, with the employee paying a further 13.7% before health.
poland||Maternity leave: 20 weeks for one child, up to 37 weeks for multiple births, paid by ZUS at 100%. Up to 6 weeks may be taken before the due date; 14 weeks after the birth are the mother's, and the rest can transfer to the father.
portugal||Minimum wage: €920 per month as of 1 January 2026, paid across 14 months, up from €870 in 2025.
portugal||Social security: Employer social security is 23.75% of gross pay, against 11% from the employee, plus a small work-compensation fund contribution.
portugal||Notice period: Set by the Labour Code and scaled by service: 15 days under a year, 30 days from one to five years, 60 days from five to ten, and 75 days beyond ten years. Collective agreements can lengthen it.
puerto-rico||Minimum wage: $10.50 per hour as of 2026. Tipped employees: minimum cash wage $8.63 per hour.
US DOL state minimum wage table, 2026
puerto-rico||Paid time off: Vacation accrues monthly and sick leave accrues one day a month, for employees working at least 130 hours in the month. For those hired after 26 January 2017 the vacation rate rises with service, from half a day a month in year one to one and a quarter days after fifteen years; employers with twelve or fewer employees accrue half a day a month.
Act 4-2017 (LTFA) as reinstated after Act 41-2022 was voided · Jackson Lewis, Littler
puerto-rico||Public holidays: Federal holidays apply, and Puerto Rico adds its own — among them Three Kings Day, Emancipation Day, José de Diego Day, Muñoz Rivera Day and Discovery Day — so the observed list runs well beyond the mainland's.
Puerto Rico Department of Labor holiday schedule
puerto-rico||Maternity leave: Eight weeks of fully paid maternity leave under the Working Mothers Protection Act — four weeks before the birth and four after — for every woman employee regardless of employer size, with the full eight weeks advanced at the start of leave.
Act 3 of 1942, Working Mothers Protection Act
puerto-rico||Severance: Unjust dismissal carries the statutory indemnity known as the mesada. For employees hired on or after 26 January 2017 it is three months' salary plus two weeks' salary for each full year of service, capped at nine months.
Act 80 of 1976 as amended by Act 4-2017
romania||Social security: The burden sits mostly on the employee: 25% CAS for social insurance and 10% CASS for health, with a flat 10% income tax after. The employer pays the 2.25% labour insurance contribution (CAM), plus an extra 4% or 8% CAS where working conditions are classified as difficult or special.
romania||Sick leave: The employer pays the first five working days of sick leave; the health insurance fund covers the rest, generally at 75% of the reference base.
serbia||Social security: Employer contributions are about 15.15% of gross across pension and health, with the employee paying a further 19.9%.
singapore||Minimum wage: No universal minimum wage. Progressive Wage Model floors apply in specified sectors such as cleaning, security, landscaping and retail.
singapore||Social security: CPF is the employer's main contribution at up to 17% of wages, but it applies only to citizens and permanent residents. Foreign employees are outside CPF entirely; employers instead pay foreign worker levies where a work pass requires one.
Trading Economics employer contribution table, 2026; CPF Board
south-africa||Social security: Statutory payroll contributions are light: 1% UIF matched by the employee, plus the 1% skills development levy for employers above the payroll threshold. Retirement funding is by contract, not statute.
Trading Economics employer contribution table, 2026; SARS
south-africa||Maternity leave: Four consecutive months. The employer is not obliged to pay it: the employee claims UIF at about 66% of earnings for up to 121 days, and employers commonly top the first weeks up to full pay by contract.
Basic Conditions of Employment Act; Unemployment Insurance Act
south-korea||Working hours: A 40-hour standard week with a statutory cap of 52 hours including overtime, phased by employer size. Employers must give a paid weekly rest day.
south-korea||Social security: Four insurances, employer-matched. From January 2026 the national pension is 9.5% split evenly (4.75% each), health insurance is 7.19% split evenly with long-term care at 13.14% of the health premium, plus employment insurance and industrial accident insurance carried by the employer. Employer cost lands around 10% to 11% of salary.
spain||Minimum wage: SMI is €1,221 gross per month for 2026, paid in 14 instalments — €17,094 a year, up 3.1% on 2025 and applied retroactively from January.
spain||Social security: Employer social security is about 30.65% of gross across common contingencies, unemployment, the wage guarantee fund and training, with contribution ceilings that rise each year.
sweden||Overtime: No statutory overtime premium. Overtime pay, and the ceiling on overtime hours, come from the collective agreement covering the role — typically 50% to 100% above the hourly rate depending on when the hours fall.
Swedish Working Hours Act; collective agreements
switzerland||Social security: Employer contributions are about 6.4% for AHV/IV/EO and unemployment, but the mandatory second-pillar occupational pension (BVG) is charged on top and is age-banded, so the real employer load is considerably higher than the first-pillar rate.
Trading Economics employer contribution table, 2026; BVG law
thailand||VAT: VAT at 7%, extended at that rate rather than reverting to the statutory 10%.
turkiye||Social security: Employer contributions are about 20.75% of gross to SGK, reducible by about five points where the incentive conditions are met, plus unemployment insurance.
united-arab-emirates-uae||VAT: VAT at 5%, one of the lowest standard rates in the world.
united-arab-emirates-uae||Social securit: There is no social security for expatriate employees, and most of the workforce is expatriate: their end-of-service gratuity is the employer's main statutory cost. For UAE and GCC nationals the employer pays about 12.5% to the GPSSA pension scheme.
Trading Economics employer contribution table, 2026; GPSSA
united-kingdom||Paid time off: 5.6 weeks — 28 days for a full-time worker — and bank holidays may be counted inside that total. The 28 days is 20 days of Working Time Directive leave plus 8 for the bank holidays.
Working Time Regulations 1998; GOV.UK holiday entitlement
united-states||Overtime: Time and a half over 40 hours in a week for non-exempt employees under the FLSA. There is no daily overtime federally, though some states — California among them — impose their own daily rules.
Fair Labor Standards Act; state rules
united-states||Social security: FICA is matched by the employer: 6.2% Social Security on wages up to the 2026 wage base of $184,500, plus 1.45% Medicare with no cap. Employees pay an extra 0.9% Medicare above $200,000, which the employer does not match. FUTA is 6% on the first $7,000, usually credited down to 0.6% where state unemployment tax is paid on time.
uruguay||Social security: BPS employer contributions total about 12.6%: 7.5% for pensions, 5% to FONASA for health, 0.1% to the labour reconversion fund and 0.025% to the wage guarantee fund. Pension contributions stop at a monthly ceiling; the health and fund levies apply to the whole salary. Workplace accident cover through BSE is charged on top by risk class.
